message: In the under-deck vertical Tuned Mass Damper (TMD) retrofit (C1), the vertical acceleration under crowd walking at about 1.9 Hertz (Hz) has needed confirmation of comfortable level, Structural Dynamics Lead and Vibration Control Specialist. To check it I used standards comparison reusing the resonant response calculation (E1) with the controlled-response stroke estimate (E6) and the detuned damping estimate (E8). I found about 0.20 metres per second squared controlled versus 1.75 metres per second squared baseline below 0.50 metres per second squared Comfort Class 1 (CL1) limit, according to Human Induced Vibrations of Steel Structures (HIVOSS), 2008. I propose holding two 200 kilogram modules tuned to 1.86 Hz as build target. My position: ready because comfort threshold is met with margin. In the concealed under-deck support frame (C2), the construction and inspection access without changing deck appearance has needed a feasible plan, Retrofit Integration Architect and Manager. To check it I used build review of the concealed mounting cross-section (E7) with clearance from the controlled-response stroke estimate (E6) and durability from the midspan stress increment (E12). I found fit below soffit with 30 millimetre clearance for under 12 millimetre stroke allowing night works from below with lockable hatches and shim re-tuning, according to French Assessment Service for Roads and Motorways (Setra), 2006. I propose bolted cross-frames installed from below with corrosion protection. My position: ready because install and maintain feasibility is shown pending joint proposal.
